comment: license_proof = HEX(HMAC-SHA256(K, M)), K = UTF-8 bytes of the licence key (grammar ^[A-Z0-9-]{19,29}$), M = ASCII bytes of device_pubkey (64) followed by appliance_id (36). cases: the server MUST accept exactly this value for the named licence, device_pubkey and appliance_id; refused: a presented value the server MUST refuse for the case named (license_proof_invalid, or invalid_field when the value is not hex64).

refused.name: order_swapped
refused.why: M is device_pubkey followed by appliance_id, not the other way round

refused.name: keyed_with_the_commitment
refused.why: K is the licence key itself; the commitment is public and proves nothing

refused.name: with_separator
refused.why: M has no separator: 100 bytes exactly

refused.name: uppercase_pubkey_in_m
refused.why: M is the field values exactly as carried in the message (lowercase)

refused.name: proof_of_another_device
refused.why: a proof binds one device key and appliance_id; it is not transferable

refused.name: proof_under_another_key
refused.why: the server recomputes with the key of the licence the commitment names

refused.name: keyed_with_the_raw_commitment_digest
refused.why: what HMAC would compute for a key longer than 64 bytes (RFC 2104 pre-hash); the key grammar forbids such keys, so this value proves nothing

refused.name: uppercase_hex_output
refused.why: license_proof is hex64: 64 lowercase hex characters (schema, HTTP 400 before any licence check)

refused.name: missing
refused.why: an activation without license_proof fails the schema (required member): HTTP 400 before any licence check, also for an appliance before spec 1.8
